delete.description:
Delete a case and everything under it (spec 06: cascades; returns 204).

The DB half runs on the writer thread: a ``case_deleted`` audit row is
appended, the chain head is anchored in ``audit_tombstones`` (spec 10 section
2), and the case row is deleted, which cascades sources, events, alerts,
indicators, reports and jobs. The filesystem half follows only once the
transaction has committed: ``data/cases/<id>`` and ``data/reports/<id>`` are
removed, overwriting the originals first when ``storage.secure_delete`` is on
(spec 02 section 4, spec 10 section 3).

get.description:
Stream the current filter result as CSV or JSONL (spec 08 4, 07 3.7).

The filters match ``GET /cases/{id}/events`` exactly, so the download is the
current result set. Rows are walked in keyset pages and yielded as text, so a
multi-million-row case is never assembled in memory (spec 06 section 5); the
scan stops at ``limit`` rows (the UI's 1M ceiling). Invalid FTS syntax is
rejected with ``422`` before the body starts, matching the list endpoint.
Top values per facet column under the current filters (spec 06).

reported with the source id and case so an analyst can act, and the response
is ``ok`` only when every source passes.

Any changed field that affects parsing (log_type, timezone, assumed_year)
triggers a re-parse that replaces the source's events, as spec 06 requires;
the response is then ``202`` with the new job, like resolve. A no-op patch or
one that only tunes hints on a source with no parser yet returns ``200``.
